Previously in the ACLIC spec, there was a reference to APLIC target registers. That's a good idea, so we should probably just call the indirect CSR "target", and it has an iprio field. 

Now the controversial idea about sourcecfg and target, which I don't think should be reflected in this PR. 
That is, provide one xiselect slot per interrupt id, and have sourcecfg[i] in xireg and target[i] in xireg2. 
Downsides are a bit more area from decoding the address, and consumption of more CSRind address space. 
Advantages are that it's much more like APLIC sourcecfg and target, and it's potentially easier for SW to initialize the control information for a specific interrupt ID. 

Also related and not needing to be resolved now, it seems to me that these register definitions would be sufficiently general that they don't need "clic" in the name, or a m/s prefix because that is already defined by the use of mireg or sireg.  

And a final naming "twist" would be to use an "ei" prefix as with the indirect CSRs that are adopted from IMSIC.
